patch.value: This candidate implements a monolithic single-command CLI (O1) that converts a folder of Markdown notes into a fully static website with tags, backlinks, and client-side search. The plan follows a thin-slice milestone strategy across five increments: (M1) core ingestion and HTML rendering, (M2) forward-link and backlink support, (M3) tag extraction and navigation, (M4) client-side search, and (M5) polish including error reporting, cross-browser validation, watch mode, and optional features. Blocking questions Q1 (link syntax) and Q2 (tag format) must be resolved before coding begins. XSS mitigation (K3) is enforced from the first milestone by disabling raw HTML and blocking unsafe URL schemes. HITL interruptions are triggered when blocking decisions (e.g., Q1/Q2), scope violations, or high/critical risk decisions require stakeholder intervention. COULD-priority features (graph view, themes, advanced search, nested tags) are explicitly deferred to post-M5 to contain scope.
